csv_project_name: Consultant for Madison Corridor Specific Plan
csv_scope_of_work: The City of Murrieta is requesting written proposals from qualified consultants or consulting firms to prepare a Specific Plan. SCOPE OF WORK FOR THE MADISON CORRIDOR SPECIFIC PLAN 1. Preparation of a Specific Plan a. Specific Plan i. Zoning (adding a few new uses to the Business Park and Innovation zones) ii. General Plan (update necessary exhibits/chapters). Please see link to General Plan 2035: https://www.murrietaca.gov/303/General-Plan2035#:~:text=Murrieta's%20Ge neral%20Plan%20provides%20a,square% 20miles%20(21%2C511%20acres) b. General Plan Amendment General Plan Consistency Analysis c. Land Use Element Update General Plan exhibits d. Specific Plan exhibits i. Zoning table for allowed (Business Park/Innovation) and any added use types. ii. Review for the appropriateness of the current goals, objectives, and policies related to new areas, update as necessary e. Circulation Element i. Provide street layout consistent with the General Plan and Circulation Element, based upon the existing Circulation Element Road Network and planned 2035 buildout horizon ii. Incorporate a Green Streets option for public and private streets as part of public Stormwater and Climate Action Plan strategies to integrate green infrastructure strategies into roads and rights-of-way using vegetation, soil, and engineering systems to filter and clean stormwater runoff. iii. Given that State law encourages and mandates the use of electric vehicles, we need to understand if the increased weight and torque for electric vehicles/trucks would require a specifically designed road. iii. Incorporation of Murrieta Bike Network f. Climate Action Plan (CAP) Implementation Measures and Updates i. Align with CAP implementation measures that are being updated (a separate General Plan Update is in process), including the existing measures from 2020. ii. Analyze and structure the Business Park zone area to have a threshold for ministerial permitting (as how the Innovation zone was set up). iii. Incorporate the Transportation Demand Management (TDM) Ordinance and Bike Network (aligned with the Circulation Element and Parks Master Plan). iv. Shading Allow for uses to include shading calculations for solar canopies to provide incentives, as we need to find additional strategies to reduce the temperature within the City. Typically, business park-type designs include more impervious surfaces and coverage of properties, and less shading due to the focus on providing space for trucks and products. We ask that standards incorporate flexibility in workspace design while encouraging innovation, so that this section of the city demonstrates how project design can address high temperatures. v. Incorporation of other proven design standards that can demonstrate reduction of energy (e.g., cool roofs, option for green roof). g. Infrastructure: The Specific Plan area does not have a complete inventory of water, sewer, stormwater/water quality, gas, communications, and electrical infrastructure. Some areas are currently reliant on septic systems, wells, and overhead 12kV power lines. A build-out analysis for sewer, water, stormwater /water quality, gas, communications, and electrical services will be necessary to ensure that the various types of businesses can achieve such infrastructure. The Proposer for the Specific Plan will need to carefully evaluate what infrastructure will be necessary to implement the proposed specific plan area (e.g., new transmission lines, existing electrical lines that will need to be placed underground, substation(s), pump station(s), and storm drains). Options need to be developed for who would be responsible for specific property improvements versus what the City and the involved providers should physically implement. In addition, it will be important to demonstrate which upgrades will be necessary to connect properties to water and sewer service and to achieve the minimum water pressure required for fire suppression systems and business demands. For sewer, it will be necessary to understand the providers needs such as a gravity sewer design or if a pump station would be necessary. It will be important to understand the location and sizing needs for the cumulative infrastructure.

title: Consultant for Madison Corridor Specific Plan
short_description: Consulting services to prepare a specific plan and infrastructure build-out analysis in Murrieta.
project_scope: Preparation of the Madison Corridor Specific Plan, including zoning updates for Business Park and Innovation zones, General Plan amendments and consistency analysis, Land Use Element updates, specific plan exhibits, circulation planning with street layout for the 2035 buildout horizon, green streets integration, bike network incorporation, Climate Action Plan implementation measures, and infrastructure build-out analysis. Infrastructure review includes water, sewer, stormwater/water quality, gas, communications, and electrical systems, with evaluation of needs such as new transmission lines, undergrounding existing 12kV lines, substations, pump stations, storm drains, water pressure for fire suppression, and gravity sewer versus pump station solutions.
services: Planning and consulting services for specific plan preparation, zoning and general plan updates, circulation and bike network planning, climate action and sustainability integration, and infrastructure analysis for utility and civil systems.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an urban/planning specific plan assignment, not a structural engineering or bridge/building design project.
- Scope focuses on land use, zoning, circulation, policy, and infrastructure planning rather than detailed structural design.
- Some relevance from infrastructure and green streets considerations, but no defined bridge, roof, tower, stadium, or complex building structure.
- Falls close to pure urban/open space planning, which is generally not a target area for sbp.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the source. The document describes planning services only and mentions future infrastructure needs such as transmission lines, substations, pump stations, storm drains, and utility upgrades, but provides no quantities or cost basis for a realistic estimate.
fee_explanation: No fee information is explicitly available in the source. This is an RFP for consulting services, but no estimated contract value, budget, or fee schedule is provided.
references_qualifications: Qualified consultants or consulting firms are requested. No specific minimum reference projects, fee zones, licenses, or quantified qualification requirements are stated in the provided source.
contracting_authority: City of Murrieta, Murrieta, California, USA. Contact: Jarrett Ramaiya, Deputy Director. Email: jramaiya@murrietaca.gov; general submittal email: submittals@murrietaca.gov; phone: 951-461-6060; website: https://www.murrietaca.gov//bids.aspx?bidID=103
notes: Target market listed as Parks. Questions deadline: 07/30/2026 05:00 PM PDT. Prevailing wage rates may apply. Solicitation documents available online. Although infrastructure topics are included, the procurement is for preparation of a specific plan rather than design of a defined structure. Category assigned by best fit due to lack of a matching planning category.
